chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Al-Ammar ibn Marvan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
There is one-fifth (khums) on what is extracted from mines, the sea, booties, on what is legally permissible mixed with what is forbidden when its owner is not known, and on treasures.
ai.seo_question: What types of wealth are subject to the one-fifth tax (khums) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the foundational categories of wealth subject to the khums levy, emphasizing the Imam’s authority over specific economic resources. It highlights the practical application of divine rights in areas such as marine products and mixed wealth, reflecting the jurisprudential distinction between war booty and other forms of acquired property. The narration underscores the comprehensive nature of khums as a spiritual and economic purification mechanism in Shia law.
